# LFS degradation for some customers

## What Changed

Nov 26, 00:43 UTC Resolved - On November 25, 2026, between 21:30 UTC and 00:28 UTC, Git Large File Storage (LFS) operations on github.com were degraded. During this time, an average of 2% of Git LFS requests failed, peaking at 4%. Many more requests initially failed but succeeded when Git LFS clients automatically retried them, which caused slower uploads and downloads for affected users. Other Git operations were not affected. This was due to a large volume of automated, unauthenticated traffic that overwhelmed the Git LFS servers in one of our regions, leaving them unable to respond to requests in time. We mitigated the incident by moving most Git LFS traffic from the affected region to other regions with more capacity. Error rates returned to normal by 00:28 UTC. We are working to limit the impact of high-volume unauthenticated traffic on Git LFS, and to add capacity in the affected region, to prevent similar disruptions in the future. Nov 26, 00:41 UTC Monitoring - The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability. Nov 26, 00:28 UTC Update - We've applied a mitigation to fix the issues in Git LFS.
